headline: RBI deletes limits on non-option derivative contracts for commercial banks
summary_points: RBI issued the Commercial Banks - Miscellaneous Second Amendment Directions, 2026 under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Section C 'Limits for Non-Option Derivative Contracts' in Chapter IV of the 2025 Directions (paragraph 37) stands deleted.
The amendment comes into effect immediately upon issuance.
The notification does not state any replacement framework or reasons beyond a 'review'.
who_is_affected: Commercial banks that deal in non-option derivative contracts, and their treasury, compliance and risk teams.
action_required: Review the full RBI direction, update internal derivative limit policies and compliance checklists, and confirm what, if any, other limits still apply.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Miscellaneous) Second Amendment Directions, 2026 (RBI/2026-27/294, dated October 19, 2026).

What has changed:
Section C on 'Limits for Non-Option Derivative Contracts' in Chapter IV of the Commercial Banks - Miscellaneous Directions, 2025 (paragraph 37) stands deleted.

The amendment is issued under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, following a review, and takes effect immediately upon issuance.

Why it matters:
Banks, treasury teams, risk and compliance professionals and their advisers should re-check internal policies, limit frameworks and board-approved derivative policies that referred to this section.

The notification does not itself set out a replacement framework, so it is worth checking for any related RBI directions that continue to apply.

Please verify the details with the official RBI notification before acting.
